title: Power Automate process mining: export object-centric models to a Microsoft Fabric semantic model
summary: Hold: the automation column presents a read-only tenant-settings API as the equivalent of a setting that controls access. The prose also treats published process-mining workspace prerequisites as unconfirmed despite Microsoft's guidance covering connections to the process mining capability. The cited Learn pages opened successfully in this check.

claims.claim: Power Automate Process Mining supports exporting object-centric process mining results to Microsoft Fabric semantic models.
claims.quote: It enables direct publishing of object-centric process mining (OCPM) results into Microsoft Fabric semantic models

claims.claim: Publishing creates a new Direct Lake semantic model.
claims.quote: When you publish a process to Fabric workspace, it creates a new DirectLake semantic model

claims.claim: Exported process data is stored in Fabric Lakehouse delta tables beneath the semantic model.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The maker chooses an available Fabric workspace.
claims.quote: Select from the list of available Fabric workspaces.

claims.claim: The maker chooses a Fabric Lakehouse in that workspace.
claims.quote: Select a Fabric Lakehouse in the workspace.

claims.claim: The maker chooses a name for the default report.
claims.quote: Select a name for the default report that will be created for the resulting semantic model.

claims.claim: The model includes object types and objects with ingested object attributes.
claims.quote: Object Types | List of all types of objects in the process. ... Objects | List of all objects ... relevant object level attributes as additional columns (when ingested).

claims.claim: The model includes events and ingested event-level attributes.
claims.quote: Events | Entity holds list of all events in the process ... ingested event level attributes as additional columns.

claims.claim: The model includes relations between events and objects.
claims.quote: EventObjectRelations | Entity holds all relationships between Events and Objects "touched" by the execution of an event.

claims.claim: The model includes derived nodes used for visuals.
claims.quote: Visuals data entities ... include items derived from the raw data by process mining algorithms ... Nodes | Entity holds all nodes with reference to specific object

claims.claim: The model includes derived edges used for visuals.
claims.quote: Edges | Entity holds all edges identified between nodes with reference to particular object, nodes and including the relevant calculated measures.

claims.claim: The model includes process executions based on a leading object type.
claims.quote: Process execution data entities are calculated as process instances of interconnected objects based on a leading object type.

claims.claim: The model includes predefined relationships.
claims.quote: The published data model includes predefined relationships that handle filtering and interconnectivity of visuals.

claims.claim: Some relationships are hidden.
claims.quote: Some relationships are hidden in the model.

claims.claim: Only one relationship between the same two tables can be active.
claims.quote: This limitation exists because only one relationship between the same two tables can be active in semantic models.

claims.claim: Lakehouse column sanitisation retains English letters, digits and underscores.
claims.quote: Allowed characters include: a-z: lowercase English letters; A-Z: uppercase English letters; 0-9: digits; _: underscore

claims.claim: Other characters in Lakehouse column names are replaced with underscores.
claims.quote: All other characters are replaced with an underscore (_) as part of the sanitization process.

claims.claim: Semantic-model columns retain their original names.
claims.quote: Lakehouse delta table columns therefore use the sanitized column names, whereas semantic model columns use the original column names.

claims.claim: Export can be interrupted by column-name collisions such as Customer_Name and Customer Name.
claims.quote: export isn't successful, as the ingested data source includes two columns that result in identical names after sanitization ... Customer_Name and Customer Name.

claims.claim: A column-name collision produces a specific error message for the user.
claims.quote: The export is interrupted and user is notified with the specific error message.

claims.claim: After publishing, Process Mining automatically keeps the semantic model up to date by default.
claims.quote: By default, Power Automate Process Mining automatically keeps the semantic model up to date.

claims.claim: The semantic model Settings screen contains the Keep your Direct Lake data up to date flag, which can be turned off.
claims.quote: turning off the Keep your Direct Lake data up to date flag in the Settings screen of the semantic model.

claims.claim: Changing that screen requires taking ownership using Take over first.
claims.quote: Before you update this screen, you need to take ownership of the semantic model by selecting Take over at the top of the Settings screen.
